content.title: About
content.content: Walnuts are the edible seeds of trees of the genus Juglans, most commonly the English or Persian walnut (Juglans regia), native to Central Asia and the Middle East. They are encased in a hard shell inside a green husk and have a wrinkled, brain-like shape. Walnuts have a rich, slightly bitter, earthy flavor and are eaten as a snack and used in baking, salads, sauces, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Walnuts are among the oldest tree foods known and have been cultivated for thousands of years.
They contain more plant-based omega-3 fatty acids (ALA) than most other nuts.
Black walnuts are a different species with a stronger flavor and a very hard shell.
The walnut's wrinkled shape has long been compared to the human brain.
Walnut oil is used in cooking, especially as a finishing oil.

items.title: Rich in ALA omega-3
items.content: Walnuts are one of the best plant sources of alpha-linolenic acid, an omega-3 fatty acid.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Walnuts contain polyphenols, especially in their papery skin, with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Provides fiber and protein
items.content: Walnuts contribute fiber and plant protein, which support fullness.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Walnuts contain magnesium, copper, and manganese.

items.title: Heart-friendly fats
items.content: Walnuts contain mostly polyunsaturated fats, which can be part of a heart-friendly diet.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Walnuts can cause allergic reactions, which may be severe in some people.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Walnuts are calorie-dense, so portions should be moderate.

items.title: Rancidity and mold
items.content: Old walnuts can turn rancid, and moldy nuts can contain harmful toxins and should be discarded.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole walnuts are not suitable for young children because they can cause choking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Walnuts can be eaten as a snack, chopped into salads, oatmeal, yogurt, and baked goods such as banana bread and brownies, or ground into sauces and pesto. Toasting them lightly brings out their flavor and reduces bitterness. Choose unsalted walnuts when possible.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store shelled walnuts in an airtight container in the refrigerator or freezer, where their oils stay fresh for longer. Walnuts in the shell keep for several months in a cool, dry place. Discard walnuts that smell rancid or taste bitter, or that look moldy.
